title: Y1BG--FY27 NRM - EHRM Base  630-22-700 EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades - Manhattan VAMC
agency: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF > VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF > PCAC HEALTH INFORMATION (36C776)
description:
SYNOPSIS:
INTRODUCTION: 
This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC), is conducting a market survey and seeking potential sources for the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades Construction Project at the Margaret Cochran Corbin VA Campus in New York, NY.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
This project will provide infrastructure upgrades required to support the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) system at the Margaret Cochran Corbin VA Campus in New York, NY. Located within a dense, landlocked urban block, the medical center presents significant logistical and coordination challenges, including constrained access, deliveries, staging, hoisting, worker parking, material storage, and exterior work near existing flood barriers. The scope includes relocation and construction of a new campus data center; renovation of 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures; installation and certification of Category 6A cabling, data outlets, horizontal pathways, and patch panels; campus-wide fiber upgrades, redundant fiber pathways, and WAN pathway improvements; normal and emergency electrical distribution upgrades, including grounding, bonding, and 2N uninterruptible power supply and downstream electrical distribution redundancy for the data center; dedicated cooling and mechanical system upgrades supporting critical IT infrastructure, including a standalone chilled water system designed for continuous, year-round operation and ductless fan coil units serving telecommunications spaces; fire alarm and suppression upgrades, including clean-agent provisions, early detection, supervised controls, emergency lighting, and emergency power and HVAC shutoffs within the data center; physical security improvements; rooftop equipment protection and enclosures; selective demolition and construction; restoration of interior finishes; civil coordination; and hazardous material abatement.
The relocated data center will function as the campus telecommunications hub and will require carefully sequenced construction, system testing, equipment migration, and cutover activities to maintain uninterrupted healthcare operations. Work will be performed in occupied healthcare facilities located in Buildings 1, 2, 3, and 6 and will require phased construction, controlled access, and close coordination with clinical departments, VA Information Technology personnel, station space committees, project teams, third-party service providers, and other ongoing station construction projects. Renovation of the 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures will require phased access throughout the occupied buildings and coordination of room-size and equipment requirements to meet Infrastructure Standards and Technology Services (ISTS) requirements. 
PROCUREMENT INFORMATION:
The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price construction contract utilizing the design-bid-build delivery method (final specifications and drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued either as a Request for Proposals (RFP) in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 15, considering technical and price factors, or as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) in accordance with RFO Part 14, considering price only. The results of this market research will assist the Government in determining the final procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information obtained during the market research process.
The anticipated solicitation is currently planned for release in February 2027. The magnitude of construction is between $40,000,000.00 and $50,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 (size standard $45.0 million) applies to this procurement. The anticipated period of performance is 960 calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The contractor will provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and other resources necessary to complete the project in accordance with the contract documents prepared by an independent architect-engineer firm.
CAPABILITY STATEMENT:
Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: 
Section 1: Provide the company name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, point-of-contact name, telephone number, and email address.
Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, HUBZone Small Business, etc.). 
Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. 
Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above.
Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: 
No more than three (3) contracts that your company has performed within the last seven (7) years that are of comparable size, complexity, and scope to this requirement. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates.
